payload.data: Night of 16/17 May 1943. Nineteen Lancaster B.III (Type 464 Provisioning) of 617 Squadron, each carrying one 9,250 lb Upkeep mine, are to breach the Ruhr dams: Möhne (X), Eder (Y) and Sorpe (Z), with Lister, Ennepe and Diemel as last resorts. Upkeep is spun backwards at 500 rpm and dropped at 60 ft and 220 mph, 400–450 yards short of the wall. Clock: British Double Summer Time, UTC+2, as was German summer time.

21:28–21:31: the second wave — Barlow, Munro, Byers, Rice — leaves Scampton singly for the Sorpe by the northern route over Vlieland and the IJsselmeer, timed to cross the enemy coast with the first wave. McCarthy, the fifth, is delayed changing to the spare aircraft AJ-T.

21:39: Gibson, Hopgood and Martin take off in a vic; Young, Maltby and Shannon follow at 21:47. Under 1,500 ft over England, then 60 ft on the spotlight altimeter over the sea. Take-off direction and slots on the grass field are reconstructed.
21:59: Maudslay, Astell and Knight. 22:01: McCarthy, who "took off 20 mins. late", his own AJ-Q unserviceable and the spare's compass deviation card missing.
About 22:54: light flak at Vlieland hits Munro's AJ-W and knocks out the intercom. Unable to direct his crew, he turns for home with his mine.
damaged
destroyed
22:57: Byers, off track over Texel and climbing to about 300 ft, is shot down by flak and falls into the Waddenzee west of Harlingen. All seven are killed; six have no known grave.
Killed: Sgt. BYERS V.W.; Sgt. TAYLOR A.; P/O. J.H. WARNER.; Sgt. WILKINSON R.; Sgt. WHITTAKER A.; Sgt. JARVIE R.; Sgt. MCDOWELL H.

Rice crosses Vlieland at 22:59, then strikes the water of the Waddenzee; the Upkeep is torn away and the rear turret floods. He turns back. Of the second wave, only Barlow and McCarthy are still heading for the Sorpe.
damaged
23:50: Barlow's AJ-E hits high-tension cables at Haldern, east of Rees, and crashes; all seven are killed. The mine does not explode, and German engineers examine it the next day.
destroyed
Killed: F/Lt. R.N.G. BARLOW.; Sgt. WHILLIS S.L.; F/O. P.S. BURGESS.; F/O. C.R. WILLIAMS.; Sgt. A. GILLESPIE.; F/O. H.S. GLINZ.; Sgt. LIDDELL D.

North-east of Haltern the leading section meets about twelve searchlights and light flak; Gibson reports it by W/T and Group relays the warning. Hopgood is hit about 20 minutes from the target, he and his front gunner wounded.
damaged

00:15: Astell, lagging half a mile behind since the canal turn at Roosendaal, flies into high-tension cables near Marbeck. Knight's wireless operator logs him going down; his mine explodes about 90 seconds after the crash. All seven are killed.
destroyed
Killed: F/Lt. W. ASTELL.; Sgt. KINNEAR J.; P/O. F.A. WILE.; Sgt. GARSHOWITZ A.; F/O. D. HOPKINSON.; Sgt. GARBAS F.; Sgt. BOLITHO R.

Gibson reaches the Möhne about 00:15 and goes over to R/T control ten miles out. The others wait in left-hand circuits over the hills south of the lake. Six 2 cm guns of 3./leichte Flak-Abteilung 840 defend the dam, two on its towers.

00:28: Gibson, after a dummy run through the flak, attacks first at 60 ft. The mine bounces three times and explodes short of the wall. B.976 requires three minutes between attacks for the water to settle.

Hopgood is hit on the run-in and an engine catches fire. He releases late; the mine bounces over the parapet and destroys the power station below. AJ-M climbs to about 500 ft, a wing comes off, and it crashes near Ostönnen at 00:34. Fraser and Burcher survive as prisoners; five are killed.
damaged
destroyed
destroyed
Killed: F/Lt. J.V. HOPGOOD; Sgt. C. BRENNAN; F/O. K. EARNSHAW; Sgt. J. MINCHIN; P/O.G.H. GREGORY — Prisoners of war: F/Sgt. J.W. FRASER; P/O. A.F. BURCHER
00:38: Martin attacks with Gibson flying alongside to draw the flak. The mine bursts about 20 yards short; 20 mm fire from the dam holes AJ-P's starboard outer tank and ailerons.
00:43: Young attacks, Gibson and Martin flanking him firing on the towers. The ORB records an accurate attack; the mine explodes against the wall.

00:46, at the Sorpe: McCarthy, alone of his wave, attacks along the crest of the earth dam after nine dummy runs in mist, dropping from 30 ft without spin. The mine explodes in contact and part of the crest crumbles; the dam holds.
damaged

00:49: Maltby attacks with Gibson to starboard and Martin to port. Seeing a crumbling breach at the crown, he swings slightly to port; his mine bounces four times and explodes against the wall. 00:50: AJ-J signals Goner 78A.
destroyed

The Möhne breaks: a gap about 30 m wide that widens to 76 m. About 116 million m³ pour into the valley within twelve hours (1949 US Military Hydrology study), a wave some 10 m high. 00:56: Gibson signals "Nigger", the Möhne breach codeword and the name of his dog; the word is a racial slur. Martin and Maltby are sent home.

The flood reaches Neheim at 01:20. Its Möhnewiesen camp holds between 1,200 and 1,500 forced labourers, mostly women from Eastern Europe. In Neheim 859 die, 147 Germans and 712 foreigners. The wave passes Wickede about 02:00, Fröndenberg about 03:00 and Schwerte, some fifty kilometres from the dam, about 05:15.

Gibson leads Shannon, Maudslay and Knight, with Young, to the Eder. It is undefended but deep in fog-filled hills: each run dives over Waldeck castle from 1,000 ft, drops to 60 ft past the Hammerberg spit, turns hard left onto the wall, and climbs steeply to starboard to clear the hill beyond. Shannon makes repeated dummy runs.

01:39: Shannon attacks; the mine bounces twice and explodes, with no visible result. Maudslay, something hanging beneath his aircraft, releases too late: the Upkeep hits the parapet and explodes beneath AJ-Z. Asked if he is all right, he answers faintly, "I think so".
damaged

01:52: Knight, the last mine in the first wave, makes one dummy run and attacks on the second. It bounces three times and breaches the Eder about 30 ft below the crest. 01:54: Gibson signals "Dinghy".
destroyed

Grantham logs Goner 28B from Maudslay at 01:57 and Goner 710B from Knight about 02:00. About 160 million m³ leave the Eder; the flood runs down the valley past Fritzlar into the Fulda towards Kassel. Between 47 and 68 die in the Eder valley (de.wikipedia).
destroyed
Killed: P/O. L.J. BURPEE; Sgt. PEGLOR G.; Sgt. JAYE T.; P/O. L.G. WELLER.; Sgt. ARTHUR R.; Sgt. LONG N.; F/Sgt. BRADY J.G.

Group sends the reserve: 02:26 Townsend to the Ennepe; 02:28 Anderson to the Sorpe; 02:31 Ottley to the Lister, acknowledged. Burpee was lost at Gilze-Rijen about 02:00. 02:35: Ottley is shot down near Hamm; rear gunner Fred Tees survives as a prisoner. 02:36: Maudslay is shot down by flak at Klein-Netterden, near Emmerich; all killed.
destroyed
Killed: P/O. W.H.T. OTTLEY.; Sgt. MARSDEN R.; F/O. J.K. BARRETT.; Sgt. GUTERMAN J.; F/Sgt. JOHNSTON L.; Sgt. STRANGE H. — Prisoners of war: Sgt. TEES R.
destroyed
Killed: S/Ldr. H.E. MAUDSLAY.; Sgt. J. MARRIOTT.; F/O. R.A. URQUHART.; Sgt. R. COTTAM.; P/O. M.J.D. FULLER.; F/O. W.J. TYTHERLEIGH.; Sgt. N.C. BURROWS.
02:58: Young, almost clear of Holland, is shot down by flak and comes down in the sea off Castricum aan Zee. All seven are killed and lie in Bergen General Cemetery.
destroyed
Killed: S/Ldr. H.M. YOUNG; Sgt. R. HORSFALL; Sgt. C.W. ROBERTS; Sgt. L. NICHOLS; F/O. V.S. MACAUSLAND; Sgt. A.G. YEO; Sgt. L. IBBOTSON

03:10: Anderson, his rear turret unserviceable and the valleys filling with mist, turns back with his mine. 03:14: Brown attacks the Sorpe from 60 ft after marking the mist with incendiaries in the trees; the mine explodes on the crest, which holds.

03:37: Townsend drops on his third run in mist; the mine bounces twice and explodes short. He reported the Ennepe; the ORB editor, Sweetman and others argue he attacked the Bever, about 11 km to the south.
Townsend reported attacking the Ennepe dam; post-war research suggests it was the Bever dam nearby.

Gibson lands at 04:15. Townsend, the last back, crosses Holland in daylight and lands at 06:15. Of 133 aircrew, 53 are killed and three captured; eight Lancasters are lost. The floods kill at least 1,650 people, more than 1,000 of them forced labourers and prisoners of war. Gibson is awarded the Victoria Cross.
